## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
User-requested feature (relayed via opag, verified against source, 2026-08-31): `quest init` currently offers only a single yes/no prompt -- "Write the managed AGENTS.md instructions block?" (src/cli/main.ts:544) -- and the boolean --agent-instructions flag (src/cli/main.ts:157,672,679,691) has no target selection. The request is a multi-select of which agent instruction file(s) to write: Claude Code -> CLAUDE.md, Codex -> AGENTS.md, pi -> AGENTS.md (per the user, marked with a question mark -- UNCONFIRMED: nothing in src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts or elsewhere in this codebase currently models a "pi" agent target at all; today the module only knows codexInstructionPath = "AGENTS.md". Confirm the correct pi target filename before implementing rather than assuming AGENTS.md.

command-help.ts documents `instructions` (:46) and `agents --update-instructions` (:61) in the same AGENTS.md-only terms, so the surface used by this feature is wider than `init` alone -- scope whether those follow the same multi-select or stay AGENTS.md-only.

Fleet context: Codex is retired as a runtime this fleet dispatches to internally, but quest is a published package with external users and shipped product surface is out of scope for that retirement (same reasoning that keeps `lore init --codex`). Codex stays in scope for this feature on that basis.
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->

RECONCILIATION, found by the orchestrator while answering a user question about what's deferred: this task's title describes exactly what shipped today as QCLI-255 (quest init: multi-select which agent instruction files to write). Narrowing rather than closing -- QCLI-255's scope was genuinely narrower than this task's, on the orchestrator's own explicit instruction at implementation time ("implement the multi-select over quest's two currently-supported targets only; do not add gemini or copilot targets in this change -- growing the supported set is a separate, deliberate decision").

Why QCLI-255 exists as a separate id rather than this task simply moving: QCLI-159 was parked under the campaign's blanket defer-every-feature rule. QCLI-255 was filed and built the same day because the user asked for the multi-select directly, and a first-party instruction outranks the campaign default. That is a legitimate path, not a process failure -- recording it here so a later reader does not read "still open, feature-typed, no priority" and assume nothing happened.

Per-AC reconciliation against what actually shipped (QCLI-255, merged to main):

AC1 (multi-select covering at least Claude Code, Codex, and pi): PARTIALLY delivered. QCLI-255 shipped the multi-select for CLAUDE.md (claude) and AGENTS.md (codex) only. "pi" was never implemented -- QCLI-159's own description already flagged it as UNCONFIRMED ("nothing in src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts... currently models a pi agent target at all"), and QCLI-255 was explicitly scoped to exclude growing the target set. Left unchecked: the conjunctive requirement ("at least... Claude Code, Codex, and pi") is not fully met.

AC2 (same-file collision handling, e.g. Codex and pi both resolving to AGENTS.md): moot today (claude and codex resolve to different files, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, so no collision exists in what shipped) but genuinely unaddressed for if/when pi is ever added, since pi was never implemented. Left unchecked.

AC3 (--agent-instructions compatibility: existing scripted callers do not silently change to "write all targets"): fully satisfied by QCLI-255. Verified live and via test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts's 22/22 existing tests passing completely unmodified -- the scripted --target/--agent-instructions path is byte-identical to before. Checking this one.

AC4 (explicit decision recorded for whether quest instructions / quest agents --update-instructions follow the same multi-target model): NOT satisfied. QCLI-255 never touched either command -- they remain single-target, flag-driven, exactly as before, but that is by omission (out of QCLI-255's scope) rather than a deliberate, recorded decision. Left unchecked.

Remaining scope, narrowed: (1) confirm whether "pi" is a real, currently-relevant agent target worth supporting -- if so, its instruction-file name and its collision semantics with AGENTS.md if it shares Codex's file; if not, close that thread explicitly rather than leaving it an open question. (2) Record an explicit decision for whether quest instructions and quest agents --update-instructions adopt the same multi-target model QCLI-255 gave quest init, or deliberately stay single-target, and why.

USER DECISION, relayed by the orchestrator: widen this task rather than close it as delivered by QCLI-255. Two explicit decisions:

1. Add pi, OpenCode, and Antigravity support to the multi-select, in both quest-cli and lore-cli.
2. Leave quest instructions and quest agents --update-instructions single-target, and record why: init is the interactive onboarding path; those are maintenance commands driven by scripts and CI. The defect was that this was true by omission; making it deliberate fixes it.

RESEARCH, done against primary/official sources before implementing anything (the fleet's own "do not guess filenames" instruction), after two pre-answered objections were resolved: OpenCode being retired-for-this-fleet does not bar it as product surface in a published CLI external users run in their own repos (same reasoning that keeps lore init --codex); the fleet's "do not touch .pi/ anywhere" rule governs this fleet's own repositories, not what a published CLI writes into a user's project, and turned out moot anyway since pi's own project-root convention never touches .pi/ at all.

- pi (github.com/earendil-works/pi, fetched directly): reads AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) at startup from the project root and parent directories. No dedicated file. Already fully covered by the existing claude/codex options.
- OpenCode (opencode.ai/docs/rules/, official docs, fetched directly): "When opencode starts, it looks for rule files in this order: 1. Local files... (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md)... if you have both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, only AGENTS.md is used." AGENTS.md primary, CLAUDE.md fallback for migrators. No dedicated file. Already fully covered.
- Antigravity: genuinely different, and cost two near-misses across the two sessions researching it (recorded so a later reader doesn't repeat them) -- several SEO "2026 guide" blogs gave directly contradictory claims about GEMINI.md/AGENTS.md precedence, and Google's own docs are split across pages (docs/rules-workflows/ covers a newer .agents/rules/ folder mechanism and doesn't mention either root file; docs/cli/best-practices/ is the authoritative page and states plainly: "Create a GEMINI.md or AGENTS.md file at your workspace root... The agent automatically reads these files upon startup"). GEMINI.md is Antigravity's own dedicated file, structurally parallel to CLAUDE.md for Claude Code (which does not read AGENTS.md natively either -- only via an explicit bridge), distinct from the AGENTS.md it also reads as a shared fallback. Also confirmed Gemini CLI (a separate Google product) reads the identical GEMINI.md file (geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/, official docs) -- so the label names both.

DECISION: one new target, not three. antigravity -> GEMINI.md, parallel to claude -> CLAUDE.md. pi and OpenCode folded into the existing codex/AGENTS.md option's label rather than given their own checkboxes, matching Backlog.md's own "AGENTS.md -- Codex, Cursor, Zed, Warp, Aider, RooCode, etc." convention.

AC2's collision question is now moot by construction, not by accident: because pi/OpenCode never get their own checkbox, all three actual options (claude/codex/antigravity) map to three DISTINCT files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md). There is no scenario in the shipped UI where two selected targets write the same file.

AC4's decision, recorded as asked: quest instructions and quest agents --update-instructions stay single-target, deliberately. init is the interactive onboarding path where a first-time user benefits from seeing every option at once; instructions/agents --update-instructions are maintenance commands invoked by scripts and CI that already know which single file they're targeting via --target. No multiselect concept was ever built for either, and none is being added now.

Coordinated the shared shape with lore-cli throughout: pi/OpenCode wording agreement, the Antigravity discrepancy (lore-cli's independent research concluded zero new targets; resolved by comparing primary sources directly, lore-cli then verified the same finding and adopted matching wording), and the unconditional-availability question (quest has no equivalent of lore's detectAgentAvailability(), so the new option is offered unconditionally like every other quest option, not a new decision specific to antigravity).

Implemented and PTY-verified live: all three options render correctly (none pre-checked, per the QCLI-255 reversal), all three files write correctly when all are selected, GEMINI.md's own managed block correctly names --target antigravity in its CI hint (not a leftover claude/codex reference), skill file writes once regardless of target count.
finalSummary:
Widened and delivered, per the user's direct decision (relayed by the orchestrator): add pi, OpenCode, and Antigravity support to the multi-select; leave quest instructions / quest agents --update-instructions single-target, deliberately.

Research against primary/official sources, before touching any code: pi (github.com/earendil-works/pi) and OpenCode (opencode.ai/docs/rules/, official) both read AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) directly, no dedicated file -- already fully covered by the existing options. Antigravity is genuinely different: Google's own docs (antigravity.google/docs/cli/best-practices/, the authoritative page after a different official page nearly misled both this session and lore-cli's independently) name GEMINI.md as Antigravity's own dedicated file, structurally parallel to CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, distinct from the AGENTS.md it also reads as a shared fallback -- and Gemini CLI reads the identical file (geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/, official). One new target, not three.

Implementation:
- New AgentInstructionTarget value "antigravity" -> GEMINI.md, in agent-instructions.ts, parallel to "claude" -> CLAUDE.md.
- The multi-select's codex/AGENTS.md option relabeled to explicitly name Codex, OpenCode, and pi as consumers, plus a note that Antigravity also reads AGENTS.md as an alternative to its own GEMINI.md.
- New third multi-select option: "GEMINI.md -- Google Antigravity, Gemini CLI".
- --target flag validation (both call sites, init and agents) accepts "antigravity" alongside "claude"/"codex". Every help/usage string across command-help.ts and main.ts updated to match (init's summary/usage, agents' summary/usage, instructions' summary).
- writeInitInstructions' multi-target write logic already generalized correctly to N targets from QCLI-255's design -- no change needed there, just verified it handles 3 selected targets (uses the additive instructionsByTarget field) as well as it handled 2.
- AC2 (same-file collision handling) resolved by construction, not by an added guard: because pi/OpenCode never get their own checkbox, all three actual options map to three distinct files, so no selectable combination can ever collide on one file.
- AC4 (instructions/agents --update-instructions decision) recorded: staying single-target deliberately -- init is the interactive onboarding path; those are maintenance commands driven by scripts/CI that already know their target via --target. No multiselect concept was ever built for either, and none is added now.

Coordinated the shared shape with lore-cli throughout (pi/OpenCode wording, the Antigravity target discrepancy resolved by comparing primary sources directly, the unconditional-vs-gated availability question resolved by each CLI's own existing architecture).

Verified live via a real tmux PTY: all three options render correctly with none pre-checked; toggling all three and confirming writes CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and GEMINI.md correctly (instructionsByTarget populated for all three keys, skill written once); GEMINI.md's own managed block correctly names --target antigravity in its CI hint, not a leftover claude/codex reference.

Regression tests: init-wizard.test.ts's multiselect-shape test updated for three options; a new "selecting all three" test; writeInitInstructions gets a dedicated single-antigravity-target test and an all-three-targets test verifying the additive instructionsByTarget shape. bootstrap-process.test.ts gets a full end-to-end "--target antigravity writes and checks GEMINI.md" test mirroring the existing claude one exactly, plus the pre-existing invalid---target-value test updated for the new three-option error message (and its example invalid value changed from the now-meaningful "pi" to "bogus", to avoid reading as an accidental leftover).
